facts.text: Hillsboro was founded in 1752 in a gap of Short Hill Mountain, earning the nickname “The Gap.”.
The town’s entire historic core is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, preserving 18th‑ and 19th‑century fieldstone buildings.
Hillsboro sits at the edge of Virginia’s Loudoun Heights wine region, where dozens of vineyards and new breweries thrive on the surrounding slopes.
The Old Stone School, a historic building on Route 9, now hosts concerts and community events in the heart of town.
In 1830, Susan Catherine Koerner Wright, mother of the Wright brothers, was born in Hillsboro, a fact celebrated by the town’s heritage markers.
Hillsboro’s location near the Appalachian Trail, Shenandoah River, and Harpers Ferry makes it a popular stop for hikers and history buffs alike.
